sections.text:
On the outskirts of a vast, dark forest, there was a poor woodsman who lived in a small hut with his second wife and his two children from his first wife, Hansel and Gretel.

The family was going through a harsh period of extreme hunger due to the drought of crops, and they only had one loaf of bread left.

One night, the cruel stepmother said to the woodcutter: “We have no more food. Tomorrow we will take the children to the deepest part of the forest and leave them there. Perhaps they will find someone to feed them, otherwise we will all die of hunger.”

Al-Hattab refused at first because his heart would not allow him to abandon his children, but his wife insisted and pressured him until he agreed under duress.

Hansel and Gretel were not asleep, but they heard this terrifying plan. Gretel cried in fear, but Hansel reassured her and said: “Do not worry, sister, I have a plan to return.”

Early in the morning, Hansel went out and picked up his pockets with the bright white pebbles that lay beside the hut.

On their way to the forest, Hansel walked slowly and dropped one white pebble after another on the road without the stepmother noticing.

When they reached the depths of the forest, the father lit a fire for the two children and ordered them to wait for him until he finished chopping wood so he could come back and get them.

The two children waited until darkness fell and their father did not return. Gretel cried, but Hansel said: “Wait until the moon rises, my sister.”

When the moon illuminated the sky, its light was reflected on the shiny white pebbles, so the two children followed the path until they reached their home safely.

The father was secretly happy to see them, but the stepmother became very angry and decided to do the same thing again, and this time she locked the door on them at night so that Hansel would not be able to collect pebbles.

The next day, when they took them to the forest again, Hansel found nothing but a piece of his bread, so he crumbled it and threw the crumbs on the road as a sign of his return.

But this time, when the two children tried to return at night, they discovered that the hungry birds in the forest had eaten all the bread crumbs!
Hansel and Gretel were lost in the scary forest for several days, walking with great fear and hunger, until they reached a very strange place.

There was a small house, but the surprise was that this house was not built of bricks or wood, but rather of chocolate, sweets, and delicious gingerbread biscuits, and its windows were made of pure sugar!
The two hungry children forgot their fear, ran towards the house and began eating greedily from the roof and walls of the house.

Suddenly, the door opened and an old woman came out with a hunched back and a sweet smile. She said: “Welcome, my little one. Come in and eat whatever you want inside. I have more sweets and pies.”

The two children entered the hut, but as soon as the door was closed, the gentle old woman's face changed and she appeared as she really was; She was an evil witch who lured children into the candy house to eat them!
The witch captured Hansel and locked him in a small iron cage, and forced Gretel to work as a maid, cleaning and cooking to fatten her brother before eating him.

The witch was very visually impaired, so she asked Hansel every day to pull his finger out of the cage to make sure it was fat and ready to eat.

But the clever Hansel was offering her a small chicken bone instead of his finger, and the witch felt it and became angry, saying: “You are still skinny, boy!”

Weeks passed, and the witch ran out of patience, so she decided to eat Hansel, whether he was fat or skinny.

The witch ordered Gretel to light the large oven and prepare it, and she said to her cunningly: “Put your head in the oven, Gretel, and check if the temperature is suitable for baking.”

Gretel realized that the witch intended to push her into the oven to roast her as well, so she pretended to be stupid and said: “I don’t know how to do that, ma’am. The door is very small.”

The witch got angry and said: “You fool! Look at me, I will show you how to do it!”, and put her head and part of her body into the oven to show her.

At that crucial moment, Gretel bravely stepped forward and pushed the witch with all her might into the burning oven, quickly closing and locking the iron door!
The evil witch was burned and finished, and Gretel hurried to open the iron cage and take out her brother Hansel.

The two children embraced each other with great joy, and began to search the witch's hut, and they found boxes full of pearls, jewelry, and gold coins.

They filled their pockets with these treasures, and began the long journey back out of the forest, guided by a small river, until they found their way.

They arrived at their home to find their father crying sadly for them, and told them that their cruel stepmother had gone and left him.

The two children brought out jewels and treasures, and the father embraced them with joy and apologized to them for his weakness, and the three lived together in wealth and happiness and never went hungry after that day.
